beats.text: An eigenvalue describes how a transformation scales a special nonzero direction without turning it into a different line. This diagonal transformation doubles horizontal components and halves vertical ones, so the coordinate axes reveal two special behaviors.

The horizontal direction has eigenvalue two, while the vertical direction has eigenvalue one half. An ordinary diagonal vector has both components changed differently and usually turns. An eigenvalue belongs to a transformation together with an associated eigendirection.

Rearranging the eigenvector equation gives A minus lambda times the identity acting on a nonzero vector to produce zero. That requires a singular matrix. Setting its determinant to zero finds the candidate eigenvalues two and one half.

Zero can also be an eigenvalue. A singular transformation collapses some nonzero vectors to zero, and those vectors satisfy the eigenvalue equation with lambda zero. The input eigenvector must be nonzero; the resulting output need not be.

practice.prompt: Find the eigenvalues of A=[[3,0],[0,−2]] by considering its action on the coordinate axes.
practice.answer: The eigenvalues are 3 and −2. The first axis is stretched by 3, and the second is scaled by −2, reversing direction and doubling length.

practice.prompt: For A=[[1,0],[0,0]], give a nonzero eigenvector with eigenvalue zero. Explain why the zero vector itself is not an eigenvector.
practice.answer: v=(0,1) satisfies Av=(0,0)=0v. The definition excludes v=0, which would otherwise satisfy Av=λv for every scalar and identify no direction.

practice.prompt: Find the eigenvalues of A=[[2,1],[0,2]] using det(A−λI). Must there be two different eigenvalues?
practice.answer: The determinant is (2−λ)², so λ=2 is the only distinct eigenvalue, with algebraic multiplicity two. A 2×2 matrix need not have two distinct eigenvalues.

takeaway: Eigenvalues are the scalings of nonzero eigenvectors; singularity of A−λI identifies the possible values.
scope: Diagonal examples, the characteristic equation, and a zero eigenvalue.
title: Eigenvalues
objective: Find scalars associated with invariant directions and solve characteristic equations.
